newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Win-win situation for Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: Win-win situation for Belgian shares.

text.p: Belgian shares, which took a breather on Thursday after having set new record highs on Wednesday, are likely to resume their rise in coming weeks with no negative factors around to spoil the party, analysts said.

"The basic factors are still positive - a lot of cash, firm dollar, low rates," said Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co, who noted that the brokerage's forecast of a 1996 Bel-20 index rise to 2,300 points -- at the time easily the most optimistic prognosis -- now proved to have been an underestimation.
The Bel-20 closed 0.06 percent lower at 2,283.07 points.
Wall Street's renewed firmness was also welcome and so was the outcome of the French elections with its victory for Left.
"The chance of a broad EMU has increased. The French socialists want Spain, Italy and Portugal to be included which is positive as it gives a wider capital market," Casteleyn said.
"The fact it would give a somewhat weaker euro would lead to a stronger dollar, and that's also good news," he said.
Electrabel was a prominent loser, slipping 2.2 percent to 7,620 francs following talk of a possible merger with Tractebel, another utility unit of holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB).

A merger would be regarded as good news for SGB as it would make its structure more transparent and simple, Casteleyn said. It would also help cut the discount on the net asset value of nearly 20 percent. SGB gained 1.4 percent to 3,350 francs.
For Electrabel, a merger would mean investors would be forced to cut their stake in the stock, dealers said.

Institutional investors cannot invest more than 10 percent of their portfolio in one stock. In Bel-20 baskets, the benchmark unit for trading, Electrabel already has a weight of around nine percent and the merger with Tractebel would push it to well above 10 percent.
Tractebel was unfazed, staying locked at 15,525 francs.
Arbed was the day's leading gainer with a 2.8 percent jump to 3,960 francs following reports that steel prices were recovering.
Dealers noted that other European steel stocks such as Hoogovens and Usinor were also doing well recently and were pulling up Arbed in their wake.
